subject: general
question: In which session of the Congress did Mahatma Gandhi convince other leaders to start a non-cooperation movement in support of Khilafat as well as swaraj?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Calcutta session.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Calcutta session of 1920**, Mahatma Gandhi convinced Congress leaders to adopt the **Non-Cooperation Movement**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai: President of this special session.
 
• This movement aimed to protest against British rule, particularly in support of the **Khilafat** cause and the demand for **Swaraj** (self-rule).
 
• The session marked a turning point in India's struggle for independence as Gandhi’s ideas of non-violent resistance gained significant traction.
 
• The movement also sought to unite Hindus and Muslims, as the Khilafat issue appealed to the Muslim population.
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement** was officially launched in **1920**, following the Calcutta session's resolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement**:

 
 
• Launched to support the restoration of the Caliph of the Ottoman Empire, the Khilafat Movement was seen as a symbol of Islamic unity and was supported by Gandhi to build Hindu-Muslim unity.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj**:
 
 
• Swaraj means self-rule or independence, a core demand of the Indian freedom movement under Gandhi’s leadership.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**:
 
 
• The movement encouraged Indians to boycott British goods, institutions, and services as a form of peaceful protest against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Calcutta Session of 1920**:
 
 
• This session took place in September 1920 and was presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
 
 
• **Nagpur Session**:
 
 
• In the Nagpur session of 1920, the Non-Cooperation Movement was formally ratified by the Congress.
